subject: financial-literacy
title: Launch and diagnostic: what a need is
standards: Michigan Personal Finance foundations — introductory
Grade 3 economics and mathematics connections
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 3
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G3 Unit 1 — needs, wants, and choosing
essential_question: Why can't we buy everything we want, and how do we choose?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about what a need is, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use age-appropriate evidence, a model, or a demonstration to communicate understanding of what a need is.
Check, revise, or improve work about what a need is using the stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about what a need is.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name one next step.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
pencil or accessible response tool
play money, counters, or a printable simulated money set
printable or on-screen planning chart for simulated amounts

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “what a need is.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Model one make-believe money decision with play money, counters, or a drawn chart. Show the choice, what was given up, and how the pretend total was checked. Keep the explanation centered on what a need is. Use fictional amounts only and name the success criteria.
Complete two supported examples or tasks about what a need is. After each step, ask: “What tells you that step is right?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of what a need is and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about what a need is; then identify one check that would catch an error, a wrong total, or a weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of what a need is and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about what a need is; then identify one check that would catch an error, a wrong total, or a weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, the reasoning about the simulated situation, the accuracy of the simulated figures, and the revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Express any simulated tax or interest as a stated flat amount or a whole-cent add-on per simulated dollar; percentages, decimal operations, and fraction operations are not required at this grade. Do not score family income, household spending, or personal circumstances. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for what a need is, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain, draw, or demonstrate why the process for what a need is works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of what a need is, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking what a need is mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, no-shame language. Family income, spending, debt, and financial circumstances are never compared, ranked, scored, or requested.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Every amount, price, wage, budget, account, and business in this course is fictional and simulated. No real money moves at any point.
Never request, collect, display, or record real bank data, account numbers, balances, card numbers, PINs, passwords, or tax identifiers.
This course teaches general concepts only. It never gives individualized financial, tax, credit, insurance, or investment advice to a learner or a family.
No purchase, real account, subscription, app download, or real transaction is required to complete any lesson, project, or assessment.
No identifiable learner photo is required. Accept a checklist, drawing, planning page, learner explanation, or guardian confirmation instead.
Reflection may be kept private. No learner is required to disclose family finances, household circumstances, or personal history.
Teach that passwords, account details, and money information are kept private and shared only with a trusted adult, never with a stranger or an app.

media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile or concrete model, or an adult demonstration.
